exposure: sociodemographic characteristics (age, residence, education, socioeconomic class)
antenatal care status (booked cases, referred cases)
clinical presentation (anaemia, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy)
cohort: The study included 62 women who experienced maternal near-miss events in a tertiary hospital in Eastern India, predominantly rural, middle-class, primary-educated multigravidas.
finding: Anaemia was the most common presentation at admission (71%) and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy were the most common diagnosis (46%) among near-miss maternal mortality cases.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was the most common mode of termination of pregnancy among near-miss cases, accounting for 38.7%.
